title: Responder Guidance and Simulation Labs with Templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This document is a compact, operational reference for responders, rotation leads, and incident controllers. It combines: severity definitions and triage ladders, a quick-run containment checklist, standardized status page and customer communication templates, a blameless postmortem timeline, and a small library of hands-on simulation (game-day) scenarios and lab steps. Designed to be printed on a single page for pager responders and expanded in linked runbooks for each service.

Goals and intended audience:
- Goals: reduce time-to-stable, standardize communications, ensure actionable post-incident follow-up, and improve responder readiness through repeatable simulations.
- Audience: primary on-call responders (SRE/Platform, Serving Runtime, Infra), incident commanders, product-support liaisons, and on-call rotation managers.

Definitions and severity matrix (quick reference):
| Severity | Impact description | Target initial response | Example triggers |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Sev0 | System-wide outage affecting >95% of traffic / external customer blocking | 5 minutes | API unavailable, entire region down |
| Sev1 | Major feature degradation affecting >20% of traffic or high error rates | 15 minutes | Tokenization failures, model-serving OOMs |
| Sev2 | Partial degradation or performance regression for specific customers/routes | 30 minutes | Elevated tail latency for specific model variants |
| Sev3 | Non-urgent bugs, monitoring alerts without immediate customer impact | Next business window | Single-customer integration failures |

Responder roles and responsibilities (cheat sheet):
1) Incident Commander (IC) — owns scope, prioritization, and timeline. Starts the incident in PagerDuty channel and chooses communications cadence.
2) Lead Responder / Troubleshooter — runs technical containment and root-cause hypothesis. Runs diagnostics and coordinates hotfixes.
3) Communications Liaison — drafts status page and customer messages; coordinates with CS/Legal for sensitive incidents.
4) Oncall Owner / Rotation Lead — validates handoffs, ensures postmortem and follow-up action items are created.
5) Shadow/Support — additional engineers for focused subsystems (GPU pool, routing, cache).

Initial triage checklist (first 15 minutes):
1. Acknowledge and declare: IC acknowledges in PagerDuty and opens incident channel (Slack #incident-<id>), sets severity level.
2. Triage signals: collect these immediately: traffic/ingress graphs, error-rate, rate-limited metrics, GPU utilization, queue lengths, platform autoscaler events, recent deploys.
3. Containment decision: decide one of: continue mitigation while maintaining production, roll back last deploy, failover to fallback model, or throttle/route traffic away from affected region.
4. Evidence capture: snapshot logs, capture stack traces, save request IDs, and export a short list of representative problematic requests (see Evidence checklist below).
5. Stakeholder notice: Communications Liaison posts a short status page entry (template below) and pings CS/Account teams for customers on live SLAs.

Containment patterns and commands (common actions):
- Quick rollback: git tag -> trigger rollback pipeline: ci rollback --env prod --to <last-good-commit>
- Scale up worker pool (short-lived): rwctl cluster scale --role serving --count +50 --reason "incident: <id>"
- Isolate noisy tenants: routing rule: rwctl route update --service serving --match "tenant_id:123" --action divert:staging
- Kill runaway jobs: kubectl -n serving get pods -l job=kv-cache | xargs kubectl delete pod

Evidence checklist (what to collect and where):
- Timestamped metrics windows (5/15/60 minute snapshots) from Grafana or BigQuery.
- Representative request IDs and model prompts/outputs (sanitize PII).
- Node-level profiles: nvidia-smi, dmesg, and kernel OOM logs.
- Deployment history (git commit hashes, image digests).
- Autoscaler/cluster events and scheduler logs.

Escalation ladder (who to call and when):
1. If Sev0 or escalation within 15 minutes: oncall-frontend, oncall-coresvc, oncall-gpu, and the Engineering Director (pager).
2. If containment not achieved in 60 minutes: page CTO or oncall-ops-lead for cross-team resource allocation.
3. For data-exfil or compliance-sensitive incidents: Communications Liaison pages Security and Legal immediately and mark confidentiality:restricted.

Status page and customer communication templates (short-form):
- Status page short update (first publish):
  Title: "Investigating: Elevated errors for text-generation API in us-west-2"
  Body: "We are investigating elevated 500 errors impacting text-generation endpoints in us-west-2. A subset of requests are experiencing timeouts and failed responses. Our on-call team is actively triaging and will provide an update within 30 minutes. Impact: some customers may see errors or increased latency. Workaround: retry after 5s."

- Internal CS escalation (Slack DM / Email):
  Subject: [Incident <id>] Text-gen errors in us-west-2 — initial notice
  Body: "Current impact: 25% error rate for text-generation for customers in us-west-2. Affected APIs: /v1/generate. Estimated time-to-next-update: 30 min. Suggested customer guidance: advise retry with exponential backoff; escalate if SLA-critical. Point-person: <Communications Liaison> (<handle>)."

Customer-facing status update (progress/mitigation):
  "Update: We have isolated the issue to the routing layer for GPU pool A and implemented a temporary routing fallback; error rates have decreased from 25%->3% for most customers. We are monitoring latency and plan a gradual traffic reintroduction once stable. Next update in 60 minutes."

Postmortem and follow-up process (timeline and checklist):
1) Incident close and initial notes: IC marks incident as 'resolved' in PagerDuty and creates a skeleton postmortem within 48 hours.
2) Evidence & timeline: collect 5/15/60 minute metric snapshots, logs, and runbook actions. Add a precise timeline (iso8601 timestamps) of actions taken.
3) Root-cause analysis: at least two engineers should propose and review hypotheses; include reproduction steps where possible.
4) Severity review & SLO impact: calculate error budget consumption and customer impact.
5) Action items: assign owners with deadlines and include verification steps.
6) Blameless review meeting: schedule within 7 days, invite rotation leads, product impacted owners, and CS liaison.
7) Postmortem publication: public internal doc + summary to Customer Success if customers were impacted.

Postmortem template (one-line fields for quick copy):
- Title: "Postmortem: <short-desc> — Incident <id>"
- Summary: brief one-paragraph impact and resolution.
- Timeline: bullet list with exact timestamps.
- Root cause: single sentence.
- Corrective actions: list with owner and due-date.
- Verification plan: how to prove the fix works.
- Lessons learned: two to four bullets.

Simulation labs (game-day catalogue and steps):
Purpose: validate runbooks, exercise cross-team comms, and test fallback behaviors without customer impact. Each lab is designed to be completable in a 90-minute session.
Library (three starter scenarios):
- Lab A: "GPU pool noisy neighbor" — simulate a tenant that exhausts KV cache and triggers autoscaler thrash. Objectives: verify isolation rules, throttle policy, and rapid tenant diversion.
  Steps: 1) Create test load on tenant X using load-generator. 2) Observe autoscaler oscillation. 3) Apply diversion rule: rwctl route update --match tenant:X --divert staging. 4) Validate reduced error rate and no regression on other tenants.
- Lab B: "Model rollout regression" — deploy a new quantized model variant that increases tail latency. Objectives: validate canary rollback, metrics-based automatic fallback, and canary burn-in checks.
  Steps: 1) Deploy canary at 5% traffic. 2) Monitor tail-latency and token-per-second metrics. 3) Automatically trigger model fallback if p95 latency > 600ms for 5 minutes. 4) Confirm rollback and redeploy with fix in staging.
- Lab C: "Control-plane region failover" — simulate a region-level dependency failure and validate cross-region routing. Objectives: test DNS failover, cache warmup plan, and customer notices.
  Steps: 1) Announce maintenance window to participants. 2) Simulate API gateway failover in us-east-1 -> fail to us-west-2. 3) Observe cache cold-start effects and measure recovery time. 4) Post customer-facing status updates at T+15 and T+60.

Game-day runbook scorecard (metrics to capture):
- Mean Time To Detect (MTTD) during lab.
- Mean Time To Contain (MTTC): from detect -> containment action.
- Accuracy of status updates (were updates timely and accurate?).
- Follow-up action completion rate within 30 days.

Runbook hygiene checklist (what every service runbook should include):
- Owner, escalation contacts, runbook last-updated timestamp.
- Minimum diagnostic commands (kubectl, rwctl, log queries).
- Severity-specific containment steps (Sev0/1/2).
- Rollback and failover playbooks (including required approvals).
- Post-incident verification tests.

Rotation rules and on-call best practices (practical guidance):
- Shift length: default 7 days. Avoid >14 consecutive on-call days.
- Handoffs: always include a 15-minute overlap with written notes and a quick sync if high-noise.
- Quiet windows: define a monthly "no-incident-hiring" blackout to avoid scheduling big changes during critical events.
- Secondary coverage: every primary on-call must designate a backup for critical windows.

Artifacts retention and evidence storage policy:
- Short-term artifacts (logs, dumps) kept for 30 days in incident bucket incident-logs/<id>.
- Long-term artifacts (sanitized traces, postmortems) saved to Confluence and long-term storage for 2 years.

Quick-reference checklist for responders (one-liner items):
- Acknowledge, declare severity, create channel, tag IC, capture request IDs, post status, apply containment, collect artifacts, escalate if >60m, create postmortem skeleton.

Templates and copy bank (snippets to copy/paste):
- Status short: "We are investigating increased errors for <service> in <region>. Impact: <summary>. Next update: <ETA>."
- Status resolved: "Resolved: Root cause was <brief>. Customer impact has ended; we are running verification checks. Full postmortem to follow."
- CS notice subject: "[Incident <id>] <service> elevated errors — customer advisory"

Appendix: Technical quick-commands (examples responders use often):
- Dump logs for request ID: logcli query 'request_id="<id>"' --from -5m --to now --limit 1000 
- Show GPU metrics (last 15m): grafana api /api/datasources/proxy/1/query?from=-900000&to=now&query=nvidia_utilization
- Apply diversion rule: rwctl route update --service serving --match 'tenant_id:<id>' --action 'divert:staging'

Related runbooks and references:
- Link to service-specific runbooks (see Service Directory)
- Postmortem examples and action tracker template

Ownership and governance:
- Document owner: Incident Ops (rotation lead).
- Review cadence: quarterly review by rotation leads; immediately after any Sev0/1 incident.

Feedback and improvements:
If you run a simulation, add the scorecard results to the Game-Day Tracker and propose new lab scenarios to the Incident Ops board.

End of document.
